lines: Bloomberg tech reporter Mackenzie Hawkins uses the probe into Megaspeed, a Singapore-based intermediary, to show how advanced Nvidia chips may be reaching China and how porous US export controls are.

She explains that Chinese AI firms largely sidestep the ban legally by renting compute remotely in Southeast Asian data centers, while outright smuggling relies on tactics like declaring high-end GPUs as simple adapter modules.

Enforcement is thin, with only a handful of officers monitoring global hardware flows, and the show says Nvidia's clout is such that the Commerce Department routes all direct contact with the company through senior legal oversight.
Hawkins argues the real bottleneck is power-ready data center capacity rather than chips, and that Southeast Asia's build-out is driven largely by Chinese offtake demand.
She sees Huawei as a serious long-term rival, but says its production constraints leave it unable to meet even domestic Chinese demand until around 2030.
title: What Nvidia's Megaspeed Scandal Is Really All About
